assumptions: Continues the original loaded launch/deployment/deorbit state below its descending 90 km witness. Uses existing production aerodynamic forces and flap/attitude actuators, bank-limited descent guidance and an estimated transition from 55 degree hypersonic entry to 90 degree broadside descent. Controls, transition thresholds, rate and the 3 km diagnostic endpoint are engineering estimates, not measured Flight 14 commands. No forces, state, fuel or thermal values are imposed. No geographic landing corridor, powered landing, header-tank routing, real water contact or mission acceptance is established by this diagnostic. Model-based static pitching-moment trim blends over estimated 250-1000 Pa, using the unchanged production rotational/flap model; it is not a measured SpaceX control law. The hypersonic vertical corridor targets max(20 m/s, 0.006 times airspeed) downward with a 20 s feedback response and 30 m/s deadband. These are control estimates investigated against independently clock-read descent displays; they are not reconstructed SpaceX bank commands and never drive the clock or prescribed kinematics. The 55 degree hypersonic angle is a bounded engineering-control experiment: the unchanged body-lift/drag polar provides higher usable lift-to-drag than the former 70 degree assumption, which saturates lift-up and still descends too early. It is not a measured flight attitude.
